title: History truncation
caption: History truncation: 61 Unilever Tier A SKUs (ABC 2026-02, single) with >= 30 real sales months, 743 forecast months that have >= 24 months of history (2025-01..2026-02, 2 testable half-year blocks). Every verdict in this chart rests on 2 testable half-year blocks per k (of 5); a majority needs 2 of them. Each is re-forecast with its history cut to the last k months; the global XGBoost model (nthread=1) is refitted for every k and month on equally truncated training rows, and the same harness's full-history run is the reference. MA3 is unchanged for every k >= 3 (verified: identical forecasts), median WAPE 0.263, MASE < 1 (pipeline gate) for 75% of SKUs. Median WAPE at k = 3 / 12 / 24 / full history: TSB 0.266 / 0.257 / 0.257 / 0.257; XGBoost+MA3 avg 0.257 / 0.243 / 0.246 / 0.252. MASE < 1 share at the same k: TSB 74% / 77% / 77% / 77%; XGBoost+MA3 avg 79% / 85% / 80% / 80%. Block wins against MA3 at any k: TSB none; XGBoost+MA3 avg k = 24; block losses: TSB none; XGBoost+MA3 avg none. Current cutoffs: MA3 from 3, TSB from 12, XGBoost+MA3 avg from 24 sales months. MASE uses the untruncated in-sample naive error, so only the forecast changes with k.
verdict_detail: no k crosses either cutoff's test (2 testable blocks per k)
criterion: For TSB (cutoff 12) or XGBoost+MA3 (cutoff 24): some k below the cutoff scores W vs MA3 in a majority of testable blocks (cutoff too high), or some k at or above the cutoff scores L vs MA3 in a majority of testable blocks (cutoff too low). MA3 WAPE is k-invariant for k >= 3 by construction.

checks.detail: (a) tsb: 2711 of 2711 equal the stored values; (b) XGBoost nthread=1 full history, two runs: 2452 of 2452 forecasts identical (29 refits each; 2452 targets)

data_notes: Data note: product_key 150 / SKU 64861486, 2025-12 has a NULL quantity in Unilever_SKU_Demand_Fact_Real (net PHP 2.89, La Union source); it is counted as 0, the same treatment as the bake-off.

Measured gap, this harness (XGBoost nthread=1) vs the stored xgb_abs@A (nthread=8), full history, 2452 forecasts: 0 identical; relative |diff| = |ours - stored| / max(stored, 1): median 2.2%, p90 6.6%, worst 48%. XGBoost+MA3 avg vs MA3 in the long bin, by block: stored ---TT, this harness ---TT (unchanged). g4_thread_check.py, months 2023-10 and 2026-02: at nthread=8 the same harness matches the stored values on 176 of 176 forecasts, at nthread=1 on 0 of 176, so the gap is thread count, not harness.

Note for session 5f: the served XGBoost model fits with nthread=1 (analytics/forecasting/global_model.py:38); the stored bake-off XGBoost forecasts shown here were fitted with nthread=8 (reports/experiment_artifacts/scripts/final_models.py:81).
